newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN to set up new camp for fleeing Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN to set up new camp for fleeing Zaire refugees.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency will set up a new camp in eastern Zaire for Rwandan Hutu refugees uprooted by escalating war between rebels and Zairean troops, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Pamela O'Toole said UNHCR hoped to set up the site in the Kalima area for 25,000 Rwandan Hutus who fled Shabunda, 60 km (38 miles) to the southeast, after it was taken by rebels.

UNHCR has called for a political solution to the spreading war, which is intertwined with the ethnic conflict between Hutus and Tutsis in Rwanda where the Hutu army and militias massacred up to 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus in 1994 before fleeing en masse into Zaire.
The rebels control a huge swathe of territory in the east, where the war escalated on Monday after Zairean warplanes bombed the rebel-held towns of Bukavu, Shabunda and Walikale.

The medical charity Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Holland) reported at least nine people killed and up to 37 wounded in the Bukavu bombing. O'Toole said the situation was tense in the lakeside town but U.N. staff were continuing work.

United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Sadako Ogata, warned this week that the region's biggest refugee settlement at Tingi-Tingi risked becoming a warzone amid reports that Zaire is arming militiamen among the refugees and recruiting them.
O'Toole said UNHCR had received assurances from a Zairean army commander that military activity would be halted in Tingi-Tingi, shelter to some 200,000 Rwandan Hutus pushed west by the fighting.
Zaire's ethnic Tutsis took up arms after local authorities tried to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda.
Zaire accuses the rebels of waging a proxy war for Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda -- which deny involvement.
